auxiliary_material: The authors propose a mechanism where antibiotic use close to ICI administration negatively affects tumor response due to microbiome dysbiosis and suppression of host immune response. The conclusion suggests patients may benefit from dedicated antimicrobial stewardship programs. The study design is identified as a systematic search and meta-analysis of observational and experimental studies published between 1/1/17 and 6/1/20.
outline_action: Use this material to establish the confirmed broad negative association between antibiotic exposure and ICI outcomes as background context. Cite the reported substantial heterogeneity to justify the need for class-specific analysis. Search for primary studies included in this review or subsequent publications that specifically stratify outcomes by antibiotic class, or locate systematic reviews that explicitly address the lack of class-specific differentiation as a conclusion.
remaining_gap: The supplied text does not provide head-to-head comparisons between specific antibiotic classes (e.g., beta-lactams vs. fluoroquinolones) with reported hazard ratios for OS or PFS, leaving the first success criterion unmet. While the study confirms broad-spectrum antibiotic overall effects, it does not contain an explicit statement that existing evidence only supports broad effects without class-specific differentiation, leaving the second success criterion partially open. The reported substantial heterogeneity suggests unexplained variance that could include class-specific effects, but this study does not resolve that specific variable.
useful_material: This study conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of 48 studies (12,794 patients) evaluating the association between antibiotic use and clinical outcomes in cancer patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI). The authors reported that antibiotic use was associated with shorter overall survival (HR 1.88; 95% C.I. 1.59-2.22) and progression-free survival (HR 1.52; 95% C.I. 1.36-1.70). Subgroup analysis indicated the negative association with progression-free survival was stronger in renal cell carcinoma or melanoma than lung cancer. The authors noted substantial heterogeneity for all outcomes and found that only antibiotic administration >1 month prior to ICI initiation was associated with increased disease progression.
